findings.body: `spendOf` reads the whole session's messages and the whole ledger's delta, and `answer()` (chat) shares the session and the ledger. Durable Objects deliver new events while the review handler is awaiting a non-storage network call (for example `startCheckRun` at src/pull-request.ts:1249), so a `@andabot <question>` posted during one of those awaits runs its own model call before the review's prompt starts. Its assistant message lands in the session and its tokens and dollars in the ledger delta, so the review's footer and `review.done` report one call and a spend that includes the chat. Restrict the call count and the ledger delta to entries belonging to the review's operations (the pending's `operationId` and its `:retry` suffix), or exclude entries whose operation belongs to another delivery.

findings.body: The issue's step 2 asks for a per-model price table in code, sourced from the Workers AI pricing page, that converts tokens to neurons and dollars and shows "unknown" for a model missing from it. The diff instead reads dollars already computed by pi-ai into the ledger and infers "priced" from a nonzero total (`priced: after.usd > 0`), which is a proxy for "pi-ai has a price" rather than a lookup — a priced model whose ledger dollars are exactly 0 would report `cost unknown`. The description declares the departure deliberate (prices arrive with pi-ai bumps), which is defensible, but the repo no longer owns the price table the issue specified. Keep the departure only if the host accepts it; otherwise add the table and convert tokens directly.

findings.body: The tests call the wrapped catalog tools through `CalledWithoutHarness`, whose optional `api` and `context` parameters exist only so method-parameter bivariance lets the call compile without a fake `ToolExecutionApi`. findings.basis: At the new base, a symlinked instruction file is listed with the same blob sha as in the donor's record but without a `mode` field (the `Tree` schema in `src/github/client.ts` makes `mode` optional, and `blobOrTree` only sets it when present). `isSymlink({ mode })` is then false for the new entry, `isUnchangedFile` returns true, and `carriedBodies` seeds the donor's body — the old target's content — into `files`, so `standardsFor` serves stale content and the body is never reloaded, exactly what design.md's symlink rule exists to prevent. The mode is unknown here, and unknown should not count as "not a symlink". Treat an entry with no mode as not carriable (or default the check to "possibly a symlink"), and add a test where the new entry carries no mode.
findings.body:
`isUnchangedFile` decides a path is carriable only from the two modes: `!isSymlink(before) && !isSymlink(now)`. A symlink is detected by its `mode === "120000"`, but `TreeEntry.mode` is optional (`src/github/client.ts:215`) and the stored schema accepts records without modes, so a new listing entry with no mode reads as a regular file.

Failure scenario: the new base's tree lists a symlinked instruction file (say `AGENTS.md` → `docs/rules.md`) with the same blob sha the donor holds, but the tree entry comes back without a `mode` — a shape the `Tree` schema in `src/github/client.ts` explicitly accepts, since `mode` is `Type.Optional` and `blobOrTree` copies it only when present. `isSymlink` then returns `false` for the new entry, `isUnchangedFile` returns `true`, and `carriedBodies` seeds the donor's body — the target's content as of the old base — into `files`. The standards then serve the old target's content and the file is never loaded again for this base, which is precisely the case the symlink rule in `docs/design.md` says must load again ("A path either listing marks as a symlink (mode `120000`) is loaded again"). The same asymmetry exists for a pre-modes donor record whose stored entries lack modes, where the current code correctly refuses to carry only because `isSymlink(now)` can fire; with no mode on the new side it cannot.

Make the unknown case conservative: treat an entry with no mode as not carriable (e.g. require both sides to have a non-symlink mode), and add a test with a mode-less new entry.

accepted.basis: At the new base, a symlinked instruction file is listed with the same blob sha as in the donor's record but without a `mode` field (the `Tree` schema in `src/github/client.ts` makes `mode` optional, and `blobOrTree` only sets it when present). `isSymlink({ mode })` is then false for the new entry, `isUnchangedFile` returns true, and `carriedBodies` seeds the donor's body — the old target's content — into `files`, so `standardsFor` serves stale content and the body is never reloaded, exactly what design.md's symlink rule exists to prevent. The mode is unknown here, and unknown should not count as "not a symlink". Treat an entry with no mode as not carriable (or default the check to "possibly a symlink"), and add a test where the new entry carries no mode.
accepted.body:
`isUnchangedFile` decides a path is carriable only from the two modes: `!isSymlink(before) && !isSymlink(now)`. A symlink is detected by its `mode === "120000"`, but `TreeEntry.mode` is optional (`src/github/client.ts:215`) and the stored schema accepts records without modes, so a new listing entry with no mode reads as a regular file.

Failure scenario: the new base's tree lists a symlinked instruction file (say `AGENTS.md` → `docs/rules.md`) with the same blob sha the donor holds, but the tree entry comes back without a `mode` — a shape the `Tree` schema in `src/github/client.ts` explicitly accepts, since `mode` is `Type.Optional` and `blobOrTree` copies it only when present. `isSymlink` then returns `false` for the new entry, `isUnchangedFile` returns `true`, and `carriedBodies` seeds the donor's body — the target's content as of the old base — into `files`. The standards then serve the old target's content and the file is never loaded again for this base, which is precisely the case the symlink rule in `docs/design.md` says must load again ("A path either listing marks as a symlink (mode `120000`) is loaded again"). The same asymmetry exists for a pre-modes donor record whose stored entries lack modes, where the current code correctly refuses to carry only because `isSymlink(now)` can fire; with no mode on the new side it cannot.

Make the unknown case conservative: treat an entry with no mode as not carriable (e.g. require both sides to have a non-symlink mode), and add a test with a mode-less new entry.
accepted.title: A new listing entry without a mode carries a symlink's stale body

findings.basis: grepText checks only that record() is defined, not that its sha is the head under review.
findings.body: Failure scenario: a push moves the head while a review is running, or a superseded review's tool call races a load for another sha. `repositorySearch` loads the snapshot for whatever `pullRequest()` returns and `grepText` checks only that `record()` is defined, not that its `sha` is the head under review, so `grep` scans the new head's files. The model then reads callers whose content belongs to the new head and can write a finding whose text anchors to the reviewed diff's line but asserts something the reviewed head does not contain — a wrong finding posted, or the model misled. The new `docs/design.md` Repository search section says the tools search "the pull request's head" (#30: search "the commit under review"), and the plan's Review Focus 5 says `read_file` and `grep` must read the same sha, the head under review. The description lists this as a follow-up ("a superseded review's grep can briefly search the new head"), but the fix is small and belongs here: have `SearchAccess` carry the head sha it loaded for (or pass the run's pending `headSha` into `repositorySearch`) and have `grepText`/`treeText` refuse with `SNAPSHOT_REPLACED` when `record()?.sha` differs from it.

Tests cover the tar reader, loading, search caps, the work meter and the run lifecycle. Two of issue #30's requirements are deliberately departed from: the tarball snapshot replaces the shallow clone with `@cloudflare/computer` (documented as agreed in the spec), and `grep`/`tree` are `replay: "unsafe"` where the issue says `replay: "safe"`. The 60,000-file-cap parity test and the wrapper pass-through test the author lists as follow-ups are still missing.

findings.basis: Failure scenario: run A reaches `endOwnRun`, reads its own `pending` at line 967; the DO interleaves at an await while a newer head B runs `clearFlight` and, seeing A's record, deletes it and writes its own `pending`. A resumes and the delete at line 969 removes B's record; B's `openRun` then finds no pending and its `replaced()` check fails the run it just started. Re-read ownership (`pendingFor(deliveryId)`) immediately before the delete, or compare the stored deliveryId before deleting.
findings.body: `endOwnRun` checks ownership with `pendingFor(deliveryId)` (line 967), then unconditionally deletes `pending` and `scope`. The Durable Object can interleave at the awaits between the read and the delete: a newer head's `review()` runs `clearFlight` and writes its own `pending` in that window, and this delete then removes the newer run's record, so the newer run finds nothing pending and ends as replaced. Issue #21 item 7 framed this class of race as "whichever update lands last wins"; this change fixed the read-during-complete direction but kept it on the delete side (the old `releasePending` had the same shape). Re-check ownership just before the delete.

finding.basis: A review webhook carries incoming.headSha (src/pull-request.ts:41); the deleted guard skipped the run when the PR's head had already moved past it. Without it, a review event delivered for a superseded head starts a full model run against the new head while the push event's own review may also be running; the dedupe at :203 only fires for heads already posted, and posted is written only at submit time (:179), so two concurrent runs for the same head can both reach the model. The description states "No behaviour change intended", but this deletes a real superseded-run guard (the log reason "superseded" it produced is now unreachable).
finding.title: Removing the superseded-head check is a behaviour change, not a tidy-up
finding.body: The removed `pr.head.sha !== incoming.headSha` check prevented a stale webhook from triggering a review at all. Without it, an event for an old head can run against whatever head is current, racing with the review the push event itself started, and can double-post or overwrite the pending review. Either restore the guard or state the new behaviour explicitly in the description — "no behaviour change intended" no longer holds.

findings.basis: In awaitsResubmission the constraint ends whenever the latest transcript message is not the retry prompt. Scenario: a retry run where the model first emits a read_file call — every later request ends in a toolResult, so the constraint lifts and the model can again answer in prose without calling submit_review, reproducing the #16/#18 failure inside the run meant to stop it. Expected: the retry stays held to JSON until it ends in a submit_review call or the review as JSON. The lift after submit_review's result (test/models.test.ts:98-116) is right, but the lift after any other tool call is not covered by any test or stated in docs/design.md.
findings.body: `awaitsResubmission` holds only when the retry prompt is the transcript's latest non-system message. During the retry run, if the model emits any tool call before submitting — `read_file`, `list_changed_files` — every later request ends in a `toolResult`, so the constraint lifts and the model can again answer in prose without calling `submit_review`, reproducing the #16/#18 failure inside the very run that was meant to stop it. The constraint lifts correctly once `submit_review`'s result is in (the test at test/models.test.ts:98-116), but it should stay on while the retry is still in flight and the review is still unsubmitted, not on whoever happens to speak last. Consider recognising the retry by the run in progress or by the transcript containing the retry prompt rather than by the latest message alone, or document that the lift after any tool call is accepted.

findings.basis: When SANDBOX_CHECK_TIMEOUT is unset or unparsable, checkTimeoutOf now returns undefined (src/sandbox/checks.ts:28-31); its only caller passes it straight to RunOptions (src/pull-request.ts:606), whose field is `readonly timeoutMs: number` (src/sandbox/run.ts:58). #waitOrKill hands it to settles(exit, timeoutMs), and `setTimeout(fn, undefined)` fires immediately, so every check would be TERM'd (then KILL'd) right after starting. Expected: undefined resolves to a caller-side default, e.g. `timeoutMs: checkTimeoutOf(this.env.SANDBOX_CHECK_TIMEOUT) ?? DEFAULT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`.
findings.body: `checkTimeoutOf` now answers `undefined` for an unset or unparsable `SANDBOX_CHECK_TIMEOUT`, and its only caller passes the result straight through as `timeoutMs` (src/pull-request.ts:606). `RunOptions.timeoutMs` is a non-optional `number` (src/sandbox/run.ts:58), so this is a type error, and at runtime `settles(exit, undefined)` schedules `setTimeout(fn, undefined)`, which fires immediately: `#waitOrKill` would send TERM and then KILL, so every check on a repository without the env var set dies instantly instead of running. The description says the default now lives with the caller, but the caller supplies none — `DEFAULT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` is left referenced only by its own test. Resolve the undefined at the call site, e.g. `checkTimeoutOf(this.env.SANDBOX_CHECK_TIMEOUT) ?? DEFAULT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` (or another caller-chosen default).

findings.title: Dropping trim breaks whitespace-insensitive quote matching
findings.body: The function normalizes quotes compared in two places: `src/review/findings.ts:297` (`readings.find((quote) => comparableText(quote) === comparableText(text))`) and `src/review/incremental.ts:305` and `:348` (thread quote vs finding quote for duplicate/outdated detection). Thread quotes come from GitHub comment bodies and can carry outer whitespace or trailing newlines; findings quotes come from diff lines. Previously both sides trimmed to the same value; now `" foo "` and `"foo"` differ, and a quote that is whitespace after removing the marker is `" "` rather than `""` (it no longer matches `withoutAnchor` variants built at `src/review/findings.ts:326`). A stale or duplicate thread would be treated as fresh and re-commented. Keep the `trim()` — collapsing inner runs of whitespace alone doesn't make outer whitespace comparable. Also note: no test covers `comparableText` (grep across `test/` finds no reference), so add cases asserting that leading/trailing whitespace is ignored in quote comparison so this can't regress silently.
